D3_r3_4_apply_local.why_this_is_the_defect: Because each phase commits independently, a stella_0001 failure caused by absent successor preconditions occurs AFTER two prepared phases have already committed. The run is then neither applied nor clean. This is exactly the condition the successor contract must make unreachable.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.required_invariant: SUCCESSOR PRECONDITIONS ABSENT -> non-zero exit -> ZERO prepared mutation occurred.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.placement_requirement: The precondition probe must execute BEFORE the phase loop begins — before the first prepared mutation of any phase, not before stella_0001 only.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.narrowness_requirement: Prefer a narrow, repository-native precondition probe. Do NOT duplicate every stella_0001 assertion. The probe must cover the minimal set stella_0001 mechanically requires under the successor contract, which per D5 includes the canonical role memberships and grantor facts and NOT only the two schema privileges. A probe that checks two schema privileges and nothing else does not satisfy this invariant.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.fail_closed_requirement: The probe fails closed. On an indeterminate result it must refuse, never proceed. It must not repair, re-grant or provision anything — it observes and refuses.

uellix_writer TO uellix_app WITH INHERIT TRUE, SET FALSE
measured_evidence: db/baseline/stella_g2_roles.sql:39 — ALTER ROLE postgres WITH NOSUPERUSER ... : the postgres role is NOT a superuser on this substrate
db/baseline/stella_g2_roles.sql:47 — ALTER ROLE supabase_admin WITH SUPERUSER ... : supabase_admin IS the superuser
db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:38 — ALTER SCHEMA auth OWNER TO supabase_admin : supabase_admin owns schema auth; postgres does not
db/baseline/stella_g2_roles.sql:201-218 — every canonical Supabase role membership is issued GRANTED BY supabase_admin; that is the substrate's own established grantor pattern for memberships

db/prepared/stella_hosted_0000_managed_role_identity_bootstrap.sql:46-47,185-187 — a NON-superuser with CREATEROLE receives ADMIN OPTION (but not set_option) over roles IT creates; that is how the hosted package can grant memberships as postgres

db/prepared/stella_hosted_0000_managed_role_identity_bootstrap.sql:298 — residual risk RR-02: that installer consequently RETAINS ADMIN OPTION over every role it created, making the hosted separation 'an auditable obstacle, not a barrier'
D5_b2_grantor.why_the_grantor_cannot_be_postgres_local: GRANT <role> TO <role> requires the grantor to hold ADMIN OPTION on the granted role or to be a superuser. The local package must issue GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA auth TO uellix_owner, and only the owner of schema auth (supabase_admin) or a superuser can do so — postgres is neither. Once the five roles are created under supabase_admin, postgres holds no ADMIN OPTION over them and a membership GRANT attempted as postgres FAILS. The grantor must therefore be consistent across the identity writes; splitting it produces an incorrect-grantor failure, not a stylistic inconsistency.
D5_b2_grantor.secondary_benefit: Issuing the memberships under supabase_admin also avoids reproducing RR-02 locally: postgres does not accumulate ADMIN OPTION over the governed roles, so the local separation is a barrier rather than an auditable obstacle. This is consistent with stella_hosted_0000:98-99, which directs superuser-reachable databases to the local topology precisely because 'it gives a strictly stronger separation'.
D5_b2_grantor.local_administrative_superuser_identity: Wherever v1.0.0 canonical_privilege_sequence names the actor 'local administrative superuser', repository truth resolves that role to supabase_admin, because db/baseline/stella_g2_roles.sql:39/47 make supabase_admin the only SUPERUSER on this substrate. Recorded so the successor does not resolve it to postgres by habit.

D6_p1a_n7.no_wildcard: This is a CLOSED-WORLD enumeration of exactly three statements. No wildcard, general-purpose or category-level supabase_admin write authority is granted. A fourth privilege write under the supabase_admin actor is a STOP, never a retroactive inference from the fact that the implementation issued it.
D6_p1a_n7.counting_semantics: P1A-N7 counts STATEMENTS issued under the supabase_admin actor, not psql invocations. The three statements may legitimately be carried in ONE session applying db/prepared/stella_local_0000_local_role_identity_bootstrap.sql. A gate that counts sessions would report 1 and prove nothing about the third statement; a gate that counts statements is the control this rule requires.
D6_p1a_n7.m2_invariant_untouched: The existing per-container call-count invariant at scripts/m2-disposable-pg-bootstrap.ts:645-656 governs the M2 fixture's OWN path and is NOT amended, relaxed or renumbered by this clause. M2 remains authorized for MINIMAL_EXPORT_WIDENING only (v1.0.0 m2_reuse_decision). P1A-N7 as amended is enforced by the P1A gate (scripts/p1a-bootstrap-gate.ts), which is a new artifact. If the successor finds that satisfying amended P1A-N7 mechanically requires changing an M2 check id, count or security semantic, that is STOP_FOR_AUTHORITY_DELTA.

D7_r7_residual.statement: The historical R3.5 / MSC-07B negative-authority evidence chain is proof about the exact predecessor bytes it certified, pinned by R3_5_PG17_CERTIFICATION_PACKAGE_HASHES. It is NOT automatically proof about the P1A successor bytes.
D7_r7_residual.no_silent_parity: Parity between the historical negative-authority matrix and the successor bytes MUST NOT be claimed, implied or inherited. Establishing it requires an explicit, separately adjudicated successor certification that actually executes against the successor bytes. Until then the successor bytes carry NO negative-authority certification.
D7_r7_residual.identifier_qualification: Measured at BASE_SHA: the literal token 'R7' is NOT a live symbol in scripts/stella-r3-5-pg17-certify.ts, db/r3-5-pg17-certification-inputs.ts or tests/stella-r3-5-pg17-certification.test.ts. The nearest in-repo reference is db/r3-5-pg17-certification-inputs.ts:17, which cites 'MSC-07B.8-R7A' as the observation source for the pinned image id, and db/r3-5-pg17-certification-inputs.ts:15,52 which name the R8 terminal phase and the R8 matrix. This residual is therefore recorded against the HISTORICAL MSC-07B evidence chain, not against a current code symbol. Recorded explicitly so that no future reader assumes a live R7 control exists in the certification surface.

no reuse of this mission's own evidence claims as proof

that the forward-only branch is mechanically exclusive with the rollback file, by re-reading tests/prepared-sql-source-of-truth.test.ts:210-222 directly
that the R3.4 apply path really commits per phase, by re-reading the runner rather than trusting D3

risks_and_open_findings.A1: tests/stella-insert-policy-probe-doctrine.test.ts is NOT mechanically required at BASE_SHA (SIX_PACKAGES is a hardcoded list excluding stella_0001 and any stella_local_* name). It is retained as CONDITIONALLY_AUTHORIZED with a falsifiable condition rather than authorized outright. MATERIAL, NON-BLOCKING.
risks_and_open_findings.A2: AG-1 / v1.0.0 R4 remains OPEN: this amendment and its companion addendum are not machine-protected by DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS. Unchanged by this node.
risks_and_open_findings.A3: The Controller immutableByConvention closed world does not yet contain v1.0.12. Harmless to CI now (the count is hardcoded, not filesystem-derived) but a real coverage gap until the bounded maintenance node lands. See controller_cross_lane_disposition.
risks_and_open_findings.A4: The successor bytes of stella_0001_role_topology_bootstrap.sql will carry NO negative-authority certification until an explicit successor certification is adjudicated and executed. See D7. No parity may be claimed in the interim.
risks_and_open_findings.A5: The literal identifier 'R7' is not a live symbol in the current certification surface. The residual is recorded against the historical MSC-07B evidence chain. If a future mission expects a live R7 control, it must first establish that one exists.
risks_and_open_findings.A6: D5's grantor argument is derived from committed baseline SQL and PostgreSQL role-grant semantics, NOT from an executed probe against a live substrate — no database was contacted by this authority mission. The successor implementation must prove the grantor contract at runtime rather than inherit it as established fact.
risks_and_open_findings.A7: v1.0.0 risks R1 (fixed port 56322), R2 (LOCAL_PROJECT_ID naming truth), R3 (.github/workflows/p1a-validation.yml red), and R6 (MINIMAL_EXPORT_WIDENING unproven) are all carried forward UNCHANGED. This amendment closes none of them.
